utterances.text: It was horizontal, this way (indicating). The bus driver was in front, and that was the back part. On the right-hand side, a trench was dug for five to ten soldiers. Five to ten soldiers could fit in the trench on the right-hand side. I'm pointing to that particular position (indicating). It was right here on this side of the road (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, in view of the configuration of the terrain, we see the hills and we see that the road is in the valley, would it be true to say that with the blockades, there was a complete blockade of the Kiseljak municipality? It was completely severed, blocked?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This can be seen quite clearly, particularly after the barricade had been set up here, not on the 7th, but we were informed on the 8th. I now have a precise document as to when we were informed of this. This barricade was set up in Smajlovici, so that all the communication in the Kiseljak area was, in fact, blocked, but the main problem was here up at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did you arrive there? What road did you take? What route did you take to arrive there from Zepce?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 7th in the afternoon, I went from Busovaca, across Kacuni by this barricade here (indicating), so I wasn't blocked on that day, and I was able to arrive in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, you said that we would be taking a break at 12.45. Perhaps this would be a good moment to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We will resume at 2.45. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. If you don't mind, before we continue with the testimony of the accused, my colleagues and myself decided to inform you about a procedural difficulty that we're faced with. Let me wait until Mr. Hayman has his books there so we can do things right. There is a procedural problem that we wanted to speak to you about and to have your agreement. I'm speaking about a procedural issue which purpose is the transfer of communication of protected testimony in the Blaskic case to the Aleksovski case. The Prosecutor knows what I'm talking about. The Office of the Prosecutor appealed two decisions in the Aleksovski case, one having to do with the testimony of Admiral Domazet, which was public testimony, and the appeal was rejected, but that's not a problem. In the second appeal, which the Appeals Chamber accepted, the Prosecution said that it had the right to present a motion to the Blaskic Chamber seeking from the Blaskic Trial Chamber protective measures being, if necessary, modified or at least produced, that is, the testimony be produced, the testimony that had originally been protected, to the Blaskic case. All of this is part of the various disputes that have to do with transferring materials from one case to another, but that's not the issue. The issue is the following: Ever since Judge Riad has not been available, we've all had the pleasure to welcome Judge Rodrigues to our Chamber, but Judge Rodrigues is also the Presiding Judge of the Aleksovski Trial Chamber. Therefore, Judge Rodrigues is somewhat uncomfortable, and we have looked through the various texts, with the extremely relevant help of my friend, Judge Shahabuddeen, we have looked in and out of the texts, and we've reached a solution which is the following: To ask your consent to having Judge Rodrigues sit with us in the Blaskic case as he is, but that he also sit so that he can rule on that motion which asks that we amend the protective measures that have been given to a protected witness. After having looked through all the different procedures since the start of the presentation of evidence in this case, we are faced with this difficulty. The decision, I can't say exactly what we're going to do, but we could consider this as a routine matter, but we thought it was not a routine matter because it had to do with the protection of witnesses, and, therefore, we cannot ask the President to authorise the Trial Chamber to sit with only two Judges, since we prefer to sit with three Judges, and we have complete confidence in Judge Rodrigues, but we wanted this to be an open discussion. We're asking first for your opinion and, beyond that, to have your feeling about the possibility of Judge Rodrigues remaining with us to rule on that motion, and then we would be able to come to a ruling quickly. I don't know who would like to speak first. Perhaps I should ask the Prosecutor to speak first since it's the Prosecutor who appealed. Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours. I know the issue that is facing the Trial Chamber in this case, and before I give my answer, I would like time to consult with my colleagues, and perhaps over the break, over the 15-minute break that we have mid-afternoon, I can give you the position of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Absolutely. And Defence counsel, would you like to have some time to think about it as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If only to consult with our client, Mr. President, but I think it would only take a moment or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. What I suggest is that you inform us of your opinion after the afternoon break. Can we agree with that? All right. Thank you very much. Excuse me. General Blaskic, you can now resume your testimony. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We left off at the developments around Duhri related to the conflict of 7 August, 1992. I suggest that we continue your testimony in that regard, and whenever you find it appropriate, you may stand up and point at the model about what transpired at what point, whenever you find it appropriate. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in the afternoon on 7 August, 1992, this meeting was in progress, the meeting at the municipal assembly of Kiseljak, and Mr. Ejup Mujic asked to speak, and he commented on the current situation by saying that, should it continue, eventually, a conflict will arise between the TO and the HVO. After his remarks, I asked to speak, and I said that, first of all, we had a front towards the Serbs, that we had major problems at the fronts in Travnik and Zepce, which were close by, and that we did not need additional fronts and that the meeting itself should have as its goal the overcoming of these problems. I do not recall all the participants in this discussion, but the discussion continued, and at one point, Mr. Ivica Marijanovic proposed that the prominent representatives of the Croatian and Bosniak Muslim communities take two flags, one of which would be a flag of the Croatian people and one of the Bosniak Muslim people, that they tie these two flags together in a knot and that they drive in vehicles in two opposite directions. May I point?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The pointer, please, can we have the pointer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Now we have a camera. That's going to help us, help us see better.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: One car with these tied flags was to start from Kiseljak via Gromiljak, Brestovsko, to Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean to the first barricades?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and this was done, and this barricade was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you just take it away, this barricade.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: While a second vehicle was being looked for, which was to start from Kiseljak via Duhri, Brnjaci, Han Ploca, Lepenica, Bukovica, Zabrdje, so while this was going on, information came from the HVO sources that fighting had broken out between the Muslim village of Duhri and the Croatian village of Potkraj and that two Croats were already wounded. One of them was a commander of this village, one of the wounded ones was. The vehicle started from Kiseljak, and at the bridge in Palez, the vehicle was stopped and sent back. The barricade in Duhri, the barricade at Han Ploca, the barricade at Bukovci, and the barricade at Han Ivica remained in their positions, and according to the information we received, here (indicating), as I pointed out, here at Potkraj --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The interpreters have lost the signal for a moment. Can the witness repeat the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Apparently they lost the signal and didn't hear what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you please repeat what was the exact information you received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you speak a little louder, please, Mr. Blaskic, so that the interpreters can hear you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: So the fighting broke out, and the fighting went on at the barricade in Duhri between the village of Duhri and the village of Potkraj. Around 2000 hours, that is, in the evening hours of the 7th of August, the fighting stopped. I had a telephone conversation with the commander of the Territorial Defence in Visoko. He introduced himself as Mr. Delic, first name Rasim. He asked of me to fill him in on the developing events, and I told him about the problems regarding the blockade of the main road from the front line to the town of Kiseljak. That night and that day of 7 August ended that way, that is, the barricade remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that the fighting stopped but the barricades remained?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the armed crews, who were manning this barricade, remain in their places at the barricade that night?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That night, we had no information whether the crews remained by the barricades, but we knew that the barricades remained in the same positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened on the next day? Can you describe that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On 8th August, early in the morning, the TO forces regrouped at the Duhri barricade. There was a row of houses right next to the village of Brnjaci. This redeployment caused certain anxiety and fear among the local population, and soon enough, fire was exchanged, again between the villagers of Duhri village, whose positions were right alongside the road. They had military dugouts, and they had fortified positions there above the road, the main road between Kiseljak and Ilidza. On the other side were the locals of the Potkraj village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me just remind the Trial Chamber that Duhri is a Muslim village and Potkraj a Croatian.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And so fighting started between those two groups. In the early morning hours, Mr. Franjo Boras arrived at the main headquarters. He was a member of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and a member of the supreme command of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He requested to be informed about this situation on the events of the 7th and early hours of the 8th of August. After this, when I informed him of these developments, I asked him to call the competent people in Sarajevo and asked him to mediate -- asked for their mediation in stopping this fighting. I sat in the office while he talked with the Prime Minister of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Mile Akmadzic. He then talked to the Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Jerko Doko. The Minister of Defence asked that I send him this information in writing, including full operational details of these events starting with the 7th of August up until 1400 hours on the 8th of August, and I sent him this report, to Sarajevo. I sent it through telefax. After that, Mr. Franjo Boras called the supreme command headquarters, that is, the headquarters of the supreme command of the armed forces in Sarajevo, and asked them to mediate in cessation of fighting. On that day, fighting was intense, that is, between the two villages Duhri and Potkraj, and there was intermittent fire at the barricade in Han Ploca. As far as Han Ivica is concerned, in the course of the day on the 8th of August, fighting also broke out, and in the latter part of the day, this barricade was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was removed by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This was the barricade in Han Ivica that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, at Han Ivica. But only after fire had been opened on the part of the army of Republika Srpska, the area of Ostrik, Koscan --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps -- it may have been misinterpreted. The Serbs were the ones who opened fire.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They opened fire on the positions which were held by the Croat and Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Around 1900 or 2000 hours, an order came from the headquarters of the supreme command of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed by Sefer Halilovic. The order referred to the immediate cessation of combat operations between the TO and the HVO. Our activities were directed towards transmitting this order, and we attempted to do this via courier from Kiseljak or by telephone by calling individual villagers and the reserve police station which had a centre in Brnjaci. The problem at that time was that the Territorial Defence commanders did not show the intention of implementing this order at that time; that is, the commander of the TO detachment from Bilalovac, Mr. Zrno, said that he received the order but that he would think about the decision that he was to take. He did not explicitly say that he would not implement the order, but he made it clear that he was going to think about this order. After this, there was some sporadic fire in Duhri and Potkraj, while at the other positions, all hostilities stopped after 2000 hours. I know that Mr. Franjo Boras made another call to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic in his attempts to reach and ask for his help in implementation of this order and to the cessation of hostilities. Around 2300 hours on 8 August, 1992, we received a second order. Its contents were almost identical to the first order, and it was sent from Sarajevo by the chief of staff of the supreme command of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and was signed by Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just one moment, General. I would like to read a document. This is an exhibit, 132, D132 -- yes, D132 which is an order by Commander Sefer Halilovic, and I want you to identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me while we find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges would also like to have a copy of that order on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document which was used in the cross-examination by the Defence. I believe that it may have only been submitted in B/C/S rather than French or English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you also have it in Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is no copy in either English or French as far as our records have -- this was a Defence document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Since you've had it, I suppose you have had it translated, though. Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a Defence Exhibit, it's not a Prosecution Exhibit, and the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But that had been tendered as evidence; is that not correct? So you've had it -- well, when was it tendered? About when? About a month or two months ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: More, more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. It isn't very long. Perhaps you could read it, Mr. Nobilo. We don't have a copy here -- no, it has to be on the ELMO. All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is sent to the headquarters of the supreme command of the armed forces in Sarajevo, then there is a registration number, Sarajevo, 8 August, '92, it says "Military Secret, Strictly Confidential," and then there is a distribution. It is sent to the commander of the headquarters of the HVO in Kiseljak, commander of the tactical group 2, commander of the municipal staff -- defence staff of Kiseljak, and now the body of text: "With respect to the developing situation of the worsening relations in your territory, more specifically in the territory of the Kiseljak municipality, I hereby order: 1. Immediately cease all combat, that is, fire; 2. Bring the situation in the territory of the Kiseljak municipality to the state of affairs four days ago; 2. Seek a political solution in the spirit of the agreement on friendship and cooperation signed in Zagreb; 4. Immediately report on the implementation of this decision." Then there is a stamp and it's signed by the chief of staff of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, General, is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: -- the order that you referred to? General, is this the order which you received on 8 August in Kiseljak, sent by the chief of staff of the supreme command of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We received two orders, the first one around 1900 hours and the second one around 2200 hours. It was the same order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does point number 2, item number 2, mean: "The situation at the territory of the Kiseljak municipality is to be returned to the situation as it was for four days before"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my opinion, because at that time I did not talk to Sefer, he probably had in mind that the checkpoints should be removed, the checkpoints which had been set up after 4 August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is four days prior to the order which was issued?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. So they were up there as early as the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This order also did not result in the cessation of activities on the part of the TO groups, and upon receipt of this order, I called the main headquarters of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Mr. Vahid Karavelic answered the phone. I also asked him to identify himself in terms of his position and I also asked to be put through to Sefer Halilovic. He told me that he was at that time the chief of operations with the supreme command, and I confirmed receipt of this order and told him that for a while we had been following it and that they should mediate with the Territorial Defence of the municipal staff in Kiseljak. Sometime around 2300 hours on the 8th, Mr. Ivo Komsic arrived. He introduced himself as the authorised person, that is, that he had been authorised by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and he asked to verify that we received this order. He also called the commander of the Territorial Defence, Mr. Zrno, asking the commander of the Territorial Defence to follow the order of the headquarters of the supreme command. I did not hear what Mr. Zrno said in response, but somewhere around midnight, all combat activities were stopped at this position or this location in Duhri and Potkraj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were the barricades removed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The barricade at Duhri, I can only suppose that it was dismantled as a consequence of that fighting during that night, but the barricade at Han Ploca and at Bukovice were not removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you remove the barricade at Duhri so that we can see which barricades remained? That will be the last photograph. Tell me, in the days to come, the next day or the following days, did you have occasion to pass by the village of Duhri on the road there? Did you see the mosque? What state was the mosque in, because in the indictment, it is stated that the sacral feature was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the next few days, I passed along the main road and I visited the front line and the features there, and I saw the mosque which is right by the road. On the minaret of the mosque, from the direction of Kiseljak, there were traces of shooting, but this was damage done to the facade without any major destruction. The mosque was intact apart from that, without any traces of destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say that the facade was damaged, what did that mean? What could you actually see on the outside?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, from the road, you could see quite easily that it was hit in several places on the facade, and this had left an imprint. There were imprints, pockmarks, on the facade of the mosque, and the surface was slightly damaged with these pockmarks from shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you see any holes in the minaret?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. From the road, two-thirds of the minaret can be seen clearly, and there were no apertures anywhere except for these surface grazings or pockmarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the position of the barricade? How far is the minaret from the road where the barricade was set up?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In relation to the barricade -- I never measured the distance, of course, but I can say that it was approximately 100 to 150 metres away -- perhaps not that much. About 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, did you or anybody else, any of your subordinates, issue an order to destroy the mosque and to try and break down the mosque or the minaret?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no order of that kind was ever issued from the command, that is to say, from the building of the barracks in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Have you got any explanation or did you hear of any explanation or were you able to conclude how the damages occurred?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can only suppose that it is quite possible that the damages occurred when there was an exchange of gunfire between the HVO forces and the Territorial Defence forces because some houses were damaged as were the positions of the soldiers in the village of Duhri, and they were right below the mosque, situated below the mosque. So that when there was this crossfire going on, it is possible that a stray bullet had hit something in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In all the discussions that you had at the time, did anybody ever, up until this Tribunal, pose the problem of these two marks and the damage done on the minaret of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I personally had a meeting on the 9th of August with the religious Muslim person, Mr. Senahidin Durakovic, the Muslim priest, and a representative of the Muslim Bosniaks from the village of Duhri, Abdulah Oruc. The meeting took place at 12.20 on the 9th of August, 1992, and the priest on the part of the Muslim Bosniaks made no mention at all of this problem nor did he bring it up at all, and I had meetings before that and after that as well with that same Muslim religious man, and he never raised the problem of the damage done to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did the Muslim priest say; can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was together with the representative of the Bosniak Muslims from the village of Duhri, they were together, and we tried to find a way of bringing life back to normal in the village of Duhri. I have already said that there were several incidents which occurred between the villages of Gornji Palez and Duhri, and the Muslim priest and Abdulah Oruc told me that they distanced themselves from the members -- from those people who were --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The members of what?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The members of the Territorial Defence forces which had been brought in from outside in order to instigate unrest between the two peoples, that is to say, between the Croats and the Bosniak Muslims. I can quote his words, and I am quoting: "For honest people of the village of Duhri, to distance themselves from those who are inciting unrest between the two ethnic groups."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To close the incident concerning the village of Duhri, what were you able to conclude then or afterwards? Why did the Territorial Defence need this whole manoeuvre with the barricades and the armed guards and everything else? What was the sense of it all? Why did they do that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before I go on to explain that, I should just like to mention that on the 8th of August, sometime in the early hours of the morning, I was called on the phone by the head of the Territorial Defence headquarters, Nasid Huseinbasic, he telephoned me and asked where the commander was, the commander of the Territorial Defence staff of Kiseljak was, and I told him that I didn't know where he was because neither the previous night, having in mind the meeting of the 7th of August -- because he wasn't at the meeting on the 7th of August. After that, I was also interested in what had happened to the commander of the Territorial Defence of Kiseljak, where he was, and I tried to find out where he was and to gain information on the event. In the latter half of the day of the 8th of August, 1992, I received information that in the course of the night, the night between the 7th and the 8th of August, the commander of the Territorial Defence staff of Kiseljak was arrested by the civilian police, the reserve formations, the reserve unit at the checkpoint at Brnjaci. That means that in the night between the 7th and 8th of August, he was arrested by the civilian police, the reserve units of the civilian police of Kiseljak. It was my assessment of these manoeuvres --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Where was he taken; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the latter half of the day, he was taken from the police station in Kiseljak to the police station in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was he later released?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us return to my first question. What was your assessment? Why did the Territorial Defence need this operation? What was the goal of the operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was my assessment that the aim of the Territorial Defence operation was to link up communication from Tarcin via Zabrdje, Lepenica, Han Ploca, Rakovci, Godusa, Kralupi, and Visoko because Visoko was where the commander of Tactical Group 2 was located at the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the area of -- the region around Zabrdje and Bukovica, Mokrine, those were the forces of Tactical Group 1. They were located there. Had there been a withdrawal of forces, the forces of the Croatian Defence Council, from the front line across from the Serbs, then this communication line from Visoko via Kralupi, Godusa, Grahovac, and Han Ploca, Lepenica, Zabrdje, and Tarcin, would have enabled in full the communication line to function between Central Bosnia and southern Bosnia by roads exclusively under the control of one army or the members of one side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, excuse me for interrupting you. What was the predominant ethnic group in Lepenica? Was it Muslim?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not have any facts as to the majority ethnic group living there. I can only suppose that the relative majority was, perhaps, the Croats, that they made up the local majority. I know that Muslims lived in Lepenica, as did the Croats and the Serbs. The Serbs were the minority. The Muslims and Croats, I don't know the exact figures for those two ethnic groups. I don't know the exact ratio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me as well because this is important. The model is good, but I have a great deal of difficulty following this on the map because in order to put this back into a strategy, the accused is giving an interpretation. We still don't know why there was this operation of the Territorial Defence. I've looked through this. I've had this map from the beginning, and it's, I'm not sure, useful. I see here there's Visoko there, and there they talk about Han Ploca, they talk about a line, but it's true, I'm having some difficulty in trying to see what the strategic purpose of the Territorial Defence, specifically in relation to Tactical Group 1 and 2, which, according to the accused, seems to be the basic tactical motivation here. I have to say that I'm having some trouble here. Of course, the model is something that the accused is very familiar with. He knows the region very well, he knows it by heart, but I am having some trouble with the map. Han Ploca is here, Visoko is there, and here's Kiseljak, so it's kind of a fan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that is why it is perhaps better to look at the model, because in Bosnia, who controls the roads controls the territory, so it is important to differentiate between road and mountain because you can only pass via road, by road. You can't pass if there's a hill or mountain in the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, continue, if you could help us a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. I have tried to help out a little bit from what I've learned from this case. In Bosnia in World War II and in this war as well and even during Turkish times, the struggle to control the roads was the key to success. So if you look at the towns on the map, they are dispersed and have no links. That is why it is important to see the link between the towns and to see where the hills and mountains are, so that you can see the road and route to be taken leading you from one town to the other and how to bypass the hills, and it is enough to intercept, to place a roadblock on the road, and then you stop all circulation and you're in control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understand that it's easier to go on a road than it is to go through a mountain, that's how it is in every country, but I have seen that from Kiseljak, in order to go to Visoko, there must be a road from Kiseljak to Visoko; whereas Han Ploca is on another road further south; am I wrong or am I right? I see that the accused is very familiar with all of this and can explain it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The General is the right man to do this. Let us just wait for the technicians to switch the microphones on.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, you're quite right, of course. The main road is precisely this road here (indicating) running from Kiseljak towards Visoko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: To Visoko. All right.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is the only asphalt road that exists with a modern asphalt base, but there are other, shall I say, reserve roads, and one of these secondary roads goes from Tarcin. Tarcin is a town from Sarajevo towards Mostar. I don't know whether you have Tarcin on your map, but it is located somewhere here (indicating), Tarcin. It is the main road running from Mostar to Sarajevo. Then there's a mountain road which takes you via Suvodol, Pirin, Toplice, Zabrdje, Lepenica, Han Ploca, Grahovci, Kralupi, and Godusa, and you get to Visoko that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was in control of Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Tarcin was controlled by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who controlled Visoko?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Visoko was held by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but this entire area was under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so these are BH army positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say then that, in that way, they wanted to open a corridor between two areas controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Tarcin and Visoko, can we say that, a corridor?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This would then be a corridor and an unhampered route, completely under the control of one army which would enable --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may indicate, the corridor on the model is established in that way. So could the camera focus on that corridor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes, I see. Okay. We've found it. I've found it with Judge Rodrigues. Thank you very much, Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Blaskic. Continue. Excuse us for having interrupted you. It's not a habit of ours, but we really wanted to have the clarifications at that specific point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After those clarifications, I should like to show you a document. It is Defence Exhibit 127, which you have heard about in this courtroom. We have already used it, so it is document D127, and it is a document of the command of the Territorial Defence of Kiseljak, and I'd like to read out two points from that document. There is no translation, so we're going to put it up on the ELMO. It is from the headquarters of the Territorial Defence of Kiseljak, and the date is the 5th of August, 1992, and it states in point 1: "All units of the armed forces of Kiseljak, in their own zone of responsibility, should immediately have assignments to strengthen control in the zone/territory, the formation of reconnaissance groups, lookouts with the task of collecting, processing, and using intelligence data as to the deployment, movement, and activities of the aggressor, as well as the units of the HVO." Point 3 in that document of the 5th of August, 1992, point 3 states: "Immediately to determine the features and especially the positions on the main communication line and secondary roads for a blockade and a cutting across of territories and roads and to assign part of the forces to execute this task," so on and so forth. Tell us, General, at that time in 1992, did you know that your allies were issuing documents of this kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not. I have never seen this document until I came to the Tribunal here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this document fall within the description of the developing events as you described them? Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I just point out, point 2, it says, "Immediately engage all manpower from the units to take control of the important facilities and features in the zone of responsibility of those units with a rational distribution of all available weapons and facilities -- equipment." I would like to stress the word "immediately."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 5th, it was issued, and was it implemented?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the course of the day of the 5th, it was implemented, especially in the area of Bukovica, Han Ploca, and Duhri.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's move on. We've said a lot about Duhri today, although that is one of the counts in the indictment. Was Duhri the end incident between the HVO and the army in the Operative Zone that we were mentioning or were there further incidents? If there were other incidents, would you tell us of them in telegraphic fashion, as briefly as possible to move forward as quickly as possible, so that we can conclude with 1992 today or at least tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Duhri was not the final incident. There were more. On the 10th of August, for example, 1992, at the barricade in Kacuni --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you point that out to us, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here they are (indicating). It is on the road between Busovaca and Kiseljak, the Busovaca-Kiseljak road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the 10th of August, I was travelling from Vitez via Busovaca to Kacuni towards Kiseljak. As the barricade was set up there, we had to slow down and pass by the obstacles, the roadblocks, slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who controlled the barricade?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The barricade was manned by the TO, the Territorial Defence, and we passed by in a column. There were others in the column, some five other vehicles in actual fact made up the column, and they opened fire on the vehicle. The members of the TO opened fire on the vehicles -- on the first vehicle, and the vehicles bringing up the rear, a truck moved towards the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we can't hear the General.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- they started shooting at the vehicle I was in. I was in the front car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think that the translators have just noted that they missed something in the translation, so they are not catching what the witness is saying. I think we need to back up and reiterate what was just testified to. I don't know if it was coming across in the French, but apparently it's a problem in the English booth, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The French interpretation seemed all right. They seemed to have heard.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't quite know what happened to the end of the column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you move just a little bit or come a little bit closer to the microphone or perhaps the usher could hand the microphone to the witness. It seems to be a bit complicated. General Blaskic, could you perhaps hold the microphone? No, that might be too complicated. All right. We'll have the United Nations buy you a little microphone you can put on your tie. I'm sure that wouldn't be too onerous for the budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you just repeat, General, at Kacuni, at the checkpoint manned by the Territorial Defence, an attempt was made on you and the vehicle in which you were travelling. Could you describe this incident?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were moving from the direction of Vitez via Busovaca in the direction of Kacuni and further on to Kiseljak. At Kacuni, a checkpoint had been set up by the Territorial Defence. Before this checkpoint, a motor vehicle was parked, and as our column was approaching the checkpoint, the first vehicles were let through, and at the last vehicle from the side, from this direction (indicating), this large truck was moved in order to force it off the road, and fire was opened from the checkpoint. The vehicle was damaged, none of us were hit, but the engine was damaged. I don't know exactly what the problem was. This point is called Cep (indicating). So we had to bring the vehicle to a stop here and exchange them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Could you now please sit down, and if you can just very briefly give us a list of the following incidents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We're going to take a break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing. Please be seated. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, General, we just completed a discussion of the big incident at Duhri, and the next major incident was in Novi Travnik, it was the conflict between the TO and the HVO, and the conflict over the barricade in Ahmici in October of 1992. Between Duhri and the conflict at the Ahmici barricade, were there any other conflicts except for this attempt on your life?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were other incidents. As early as the night of the 11th of August, 1992, in Sarajevo, the Territorial Defence attacked the command post of the HVO Sarajevo, and a number of people were captured and taken away from the building of the HVO command. Several days later, the command post was freed and there were no additional serious consequences. Further, in Kiseljak, four HVO soldiers, representing that they were working for the military police, took away some 100 rifles from the TO. I was informed of this on 12th August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you order any kind of investigation or other measures?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I issued an order following a meeting which I held with General Merdan on the 10th of August regarding this matter, and with respect to this incident, I requested an investigation and taking appropriate steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you also issue an order in which you forbade that the TO soldiers be disarmed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I issued such an order as early as 10 August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: One moment, please. I believe we have a copy of this order. This is Defence Exhibit number 395, issued by the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone headquarters, and number 1 says: "I forbid any taking away of weapons or giving ultimatums to the TO units to surrender weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you please look at this order? Was this order issued in relation to that incident?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the order which I issued after a meeting with General Merdan and a meeting with the chief of staff of the Kiseljak defence office, Nasid Huseinbasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At point 2: "Written and signed warnings are to be issued to all subordinate commanders down to the squad level that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna do not stand behind such reckless actions and that they will be personally responsible for such actions." Was this what your order contained?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So will you please move on to the next conflict? Was that the incident in Konjic, which was the neighbouring municipality?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Konjic is a municipality, neighbouring municipality, to Fojnica. An incident that took place there was in relation to disarming of some HVO soldier which was conducted by the Territorial Defence soldiers of the Konjic municipality. Also, in August, there was another conflict in Stup municipality, this is one of the Sarajevo municipalities, between the members of the HVO and TO. Further, there was an incident in the territory of Breza municipality, that is in Ilijas municipality, but the incident was provoked by the TO members from Breza, and it concerned the persecution of Croats in Zupe and Cemerno who had been driven out of their homes by members of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In August, there was also an incident involving an attempt on the life of the HVO commander in Jajce?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that was also in August of 1992. The commander of the HVO in Jajce, Mr. Stjepan Blazevic, was travelling from the town of Jajce via Karaula and Travnik to Vitez to a meeting with me. He was hit from the back and he was hit in the place where he had his pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the following month? Again, if you can just give us in a very telegraphic manner?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the month of September, the tensions between members of the Vitez HOS and members of the Zenica HOS were very frequent. For the most part, it was over the issue of competence; who was going to have the command of HOS. Also, on 4th of September, special MUP units of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP, whose commander was Juka Prazina, attacked a barricade, that was a Serbian barricade, at Stup. This place is called Stup. This then, in turn, provoked conflicts and resulted in the expulsion of both Croats and Muslims from there. On 9 September, the Territorial Defence attacked the Serbs in the villages of Tolovici in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In these villages, were there just civilians living there or was the army deployed there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the information I received, first the civilians were disarmed, and then on the 9th of September, the Serbian civilians were expelled from the village and brought to the territory of the town itself and placed under the HVO control. This also involved the village of Preocica. On 9 September, the commander of the Kresevo defence confiscated weapons which were going to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to the Tuzla corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you do anything about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I ordered that the equipment be returned, and I managed to have most of it returned. I also disciplined some of the perpetrators of this act. Ivica Bosnjak was their commander. On the 10th of September, a Croatian civilian was killed in Vitez, his name was Ivo Plavcic, near the gas station which was called Kalen and was owned by Bosniak Muslims. In the town of Vitez that night, two hand grenades were thrown. On the 18th of September, 1992, I was informed that on the road between Fojnica and Gornji Vakuf, an officer went missing who was a member of the Fojnica municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I believe that we don't have that area here on the model. Who was the dominant force in Gornji Vakuf and who was suspected of having done this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This area was controlled by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Continue on with the incidents.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the night between the 28th and 29th of September, there was an incident in Kiseljak when members of a private unit abducted, that is, kidnapped Ivica Rajic, the HVO commander in town, and tortured him and threatened to execute him. On the 20th of September, 1992, members of the Territorial Defence expelled 40 families from the village of Medvjednica in the Kiseljak municipality, all of them civilians, and who had been received in the Kiseljak municipality as refugees. On the 21st of September, 1992, the commander of the Croatian Defence Council in Zepce, Mr. Ivo Lozancic, was attacked. He was attacked by members of the HVO. On 25th of September, 1992, in the town of Travnik, there was a rebellion, mostly among the HOS and HVO members, and the reason for this rebellion was their accusations that members of the civilian police were not being involved at the front lines and they did not carry out their police tasks. So there was a confrontation between the civilian police on the one side and the HVO members on the other -- and HOS on the other side. On the 26th of September, in Novi Travnik, the commander of the military police of the HVO attacked the mayor of Novi Travnik. On the 26th of September, there was another incident in Konjic. Members of the Territorial Defence attacked a vehicle which was transporting food. They killed the driver and wounded two HVO soldiers who were escorting this vehicle. On the 29th of September, 1992, there was an armed conflict in Novi Travnik between members of the HVO and members of HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you just briefly say what incidents took place in October before we move to the events in Novi Travnik and Ahmici which we just had announced?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps you could speak about the major incidents, and speak in shorter form, whether they were mostly part of the Territorial Defence against well-known people at the seat of the HVO or whether there were also attacks, because I think, Mr. Nobilo, that your question deals with the serious events of November 1992 in Novi Travnik and at the roadblock in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I thought that the witness would mention some of the more significant incidents and then move on to the two big incidents in Ahmici and in Novi Travnik. We are almost there. We only have a few more incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, please, if you can just limit yourself to the more significant incidents because we know that there have been a number of small incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So this entire period was really scattered with incidents, and that's what you're trying to show us, but perhaps you could focus on the events which, to you, in the position of responsibility that you had, you considered to be major and which have an effect on what happened later. That would be of great interest to the Judges. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. Your Honours, the following incident took place on the 6th of October. This was an attack conducted by the units of the Territorial Defence from Zenica on the Kuber feature where members of the HVO were conducting works on -- were building placements for anti-aircraft defences. At that time, we had joint defences as regards the anti-aircraft defences; in other words, the regional staff of the Zenica TO and the HVO had joint anti-aircraft defence crews, and the Kuber feature was attacked by members of the Territorial Defence and later we learned that the attack was carried out pursuant to an order issued by the regional headquarters in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now skip a number of minor incidents which were happening throughout this period and move on to the 19th of October, 1992, when you were travelling to Mostar. Why were you going to Mostar, what happened there, and what was the situation which you found after you returned from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The situation at the front, especially at the Jajce front, was very critical; in fact, in October, we launched the last effort to retain our positions in Jajce. In the afternoon of the 18th, I was visited by the commander of the municipal headquarters of the Jajce HVO and president of the Jajce HVO on behalf of the civilian authorities and requested of me assistance in personnel and materiel because the fall of town was imminent. I asked for a reception, an audience with the chief of main staff, and a member of the Defence Ministry --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me just refresh your memory. You spent October --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. With all due respect, counsel, I don't think the witness needs his memory refreshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am only doing it for -- I wanted to just refresh his memory in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You know that both parties always speak in the interests of the Judges. We all know that. I think that we are dealing with a witness who doesn't particularly need to have his memory refreshed. However, I must say that I myself asked the question a while back in order to allow the Judges to have the most synthesising type of testimony possible and to have the witness focus on the most important points. Now, if the accused prefers to insist upon all of the incidents, that's his absolute right. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let us all be reminded: Who fought at Jajce?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the one side, there were the defenders of Jajce who were members of the HVO, HOS, Territorial Defence, and the Patriotic League, and the attackers on the town of Jajce were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. So on the 19th of October, 1992, you arrived in Mostar to conduct talks with the chief of staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. The commander of the staff -- I am really insisting on the names because I have to really know who they were. Who was the commander at headquarters?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I arrived in Mostar to meet with Mr. Bruno Stojic and General Milvoj Petkovic, at the time was Brigadier, he was the commander of the main headquarters, main staff, and this was Brigadier at the time, Milvoj Petkovic. I came to visit them in the morning of the 19th of October with the intention of informing them of the situation which was very critical and to ask for assistance both in personnel and materiel. In this meeting on the 19th, at one point Mr. Bruno Stojic, who was the representative of the defence department, said "What is going on up there with you?" And I told him that as far as I knew, the only problems we had were with the defence of Jajce and that there were no other problems. He posed a question, "What about Novi Travnik?" I replied that on the basis of my information, which was yesterday's information, the situation was normal. So in the latter part of the day, I travelled from Mostar to Grude to the assistant for logistics to identify the priority materiel for the defence of Jajce. After I reached an agreement with him, I returned to Kiseljak via Konjic, and in the Kiseljak barracks, I asked the duty officer to give me any information, if he had any, about the events in Novi Travnik. The duty officer told me that there were some incidents, but that the situation had been calmed down and that there were no problems anymore. He also added that Colonel Filipovic had also called, who at that time was commander of the Operative Group in Travnik, and that he said that the situation in Travnik had been calmed down. On the 20th of October, I started out from Kiseljak on the main road via Busovaca, and at about 8.00, I arrived at this position at Kaonik. The members of the civilian police there told me that the road was blocked and that I couldn't go further on by car because the members of the Territorial Defence had set up a barricade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where had they set up the barricade?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They told me that the barricade had been set up by the cemetery near the village of Ahmici. This is the position I'm pointing to now (indicating). I continued along the road, my driver was driving and with my escort, and I arrived at the barricade. On the road, I saw two devices called hedgehogs. They are metal devices, roadblocks. I saw three anti-tank mines, and I tried to remove the mines and the barricade, that is to say, those hedgehog devices, in order to pass through. When I stepped out of the car, I heard a warning at that time, I was told to stop, and I saw in front of me, at some 15 to 20 metres in front of me, soldiers who were in military gear with their weapons pointed at me, their weapons were cocked at us, and one of them cautioned me and told me to go back. I tried to learn on the spot whether there was a commander amongst them, and I asked them who their commander was because I intended to talk to their commander and to ask him to allow us to move forward and go on to Vitez and Kruscica; however, he just kept repeating one thing, "There's no commander here. Go back where you came from." Having asked to be taken to Dzemo Merdan and to talk to him, as they did not desist in their threats, I returned. I went back to Busovaca, and at the bus stop in Busovaca, the military police conveyed a message to me and told me to contact the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak, to call them by telephone from Busovaca. The members of the UN headquarters in Kiseljak asked me to convene a meeting with Brigadier Petkovic, General Razek, and General Morillon in Kiseljak. Before I went to phone General Petkovic from Busovaca, I phoned my headquarters in Kruscica and asked them to inform me of the events because I was not able to pass the barricade. They told me, four or five members of the headquarters told me, that they had been encircled, surrounded, and that it was impossible to leave the headquarters building because 30 metres away, there were soldiers belonging to the Territorial Defence and that they were mostly from Kruscica and that they had surrounded the building, surrounded the headquarters. They also informed me --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The headquarters were your own headquarters, the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was the regional main staff, my own headquarters. I was also informed that there was fighting in Novi Travnik but that they did not have any precise details as to the actual events that were happening there. They knew that there was fighting between the HVO and the Territorial Defence of Novi Travnik and that the detonations, strong detonations, could be heard in Busovaca, almost as far as Busovaca. Later on, I tried to establish links with the head of the main staff in connection with these activities and meetings from Busovaca, and at around 2.00 p.m., I managed to contact the mayor of Vitez, the president of the municipal assembly, who was Ivica Santic, who informed me that they in Vitez had established contacts with the representatives of the Bosniak Muslims and had organised a meeting with the aim of transcending all the tensions and difficulties and that the meeting would be attended by both the civilian and military representatives. I asked him whether he had any concrete information as to the events in Novi Travnik, and he said that he knew that there was fighting there and that there were casualties, but that he had no details. The conflict broke out at the barricade in Ahmici after a shift had been stopped, which was to have passed and moved on to the Jajce front, and the military police took part in the removal of the barracks on one side and the Territorial Defence on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean the military police of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the military police of the HVO. Sometime in the afternoon after 6.00 p.m., this barricade was dismantled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where were you, yourself, located when the fighting was going on at the barricade in Ahmici between the military police of the HVO and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Almost the entire time, I was at the headquarters of the military police in Busovaca, and I was trying to contact General Petkovic. Finally, I called a liaison office in Kiseljak to carry on with this job and to try and arrange a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what the results of that military operation were at the barricades, how many dead there were on both sides, whether any civilian facilities were destroyed? What was your information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I later received information that one soldier belonging to the HVO had been killed and that one member of the Territorial Defence had been killed, who was also one of the soldiers in the trenches. I know that there were some facilities that were burnt on both sides, both on the Croatian side and on the Bosniak Muslim side, and I know that a commission was set up to investigate, it was a municipal commission, and it dealt with the damage that had been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the municipality use its own resources to clear up the damage that had been done?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The municipality of Vitez and the commission that was set up studied the damages and drew up a report of the damage that had been done, and it repaired the damage from its own resources. The members of the commission were both Croats and Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether you remember how many facilities were burnt down during that fighting.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, very few, perhaps three, and five at the most, a maximum of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened afterwards? On the 20th of April, Stojak, the commander of the HVO, was killed; is that true? Is that correct? Can you tell us something about that, and can you describe how this happened? On the 20th of October, I apologise, the 20th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I later received, sometime around 8.00 p.m., information that, in the course of the afternoon, at the exit from the town of Travnik towards -- the exit from Travnik, this position here (indicating), the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had set up a checkpoint, its own checkpoint, and at that checkpoint, there were also people who manned the checkpoint from the composition of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Territorial Defence, and that is where the commander of the Croatian Defence Council for the Travnik municipality, Ivica Stojak, was killed, and an officer of his who was in the car with him was seriously wounded. This caused a great increase in tension, so tension was at a peak in the town of Travnik itself. I received information later on at the Hotel Vitez where I was informed by the deputy commander of the municipal main staff in Vitez, Mr. Cerkez, about the situation, and he told me that the road from Vitez towards Kruscica, there was still not free passage on the road because of the barricades which had been set up by the Territorial Defence from Kruscica. I received information that at 11.00 p.m., 2300 hours, a meeting would be held between the commander of the regional staff of the Territorial Defence of Zenica, Mr. Dzemo Merdan, and I was to have been present at that meeting. The meeting was to have been presided over by Colonel Bob Stewart and Brigadier, I think his name was, Cummings, Andrew Cummings. Sometime after 2300 hours, the meeting was actually held, it did take place, and the topic was a cease-fire of combat operations in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you informed as to why the conflict in Novi Travnik broke out?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. According to the information that I received, once again, the cause of the conflict was control over the petrol station, to gain control, and over the old hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Between which sides?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Between the HVO and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us briefly something in connection to the killing of Stojak, the commander of the HVO, a very popular man. Was anything done? Was an investigation held? Were the perpetrators uncovered, and were they brought to justice, disciplined?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the killing, a joint commission was set up between the HVO and the Territorial Defence, and this was done at the level of the municipal main staff of Travnik. An investigation was conducted, and it was confirmed that the killing was performed by a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he was nicknamed Tara. The commission stopped its work, taking note of the fact that, for the time being, Mr. Tara was inaccessible for proceedings in the case to be continued. As far as I know, he was not taken into custody, and that case was never taken any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we move to another area, I should like to mention the 23rd of October. You were at a meeting in the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you received the highest decoration of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Golden Lily, and if that is true, would you explain how and when this took place?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. On the 23rd of October, I was within the delegation, a member of the delegation, of the Croatian Defence Council which attended the first Tri Partite meeting at the airport in Sarajevo. It was the stand of the HVO delegation that, before the Tri Partite meeting take place, a meeting be convened in the presidency building, the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, between the members, that is to say, the delegations of the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in order to coordinate and dovetail stands and coordinate further work. At that meeting, I, as the commander of the main staff of the HVO, and two other officers were decorated with the order of merit of the Golden Lily, and that was the highest military decoration of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For a moment, we'll leave behind chronology, and we'll go on to talk about the end of the year tomorrow, but let's go over to a summary review of crime. We saw the incidents that took place between the two sides. Can you tell us something about crime? As a concept, was this something that worried you and something that drew your attention? What were the characteristics of the crime that was taking place? So if you could summarise, in the few minutes that we have left, and explain to the Court what crime represented in the area of Central Bosnia in 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The position of this area of Central Bosnia, and when I say that, I have in mind Kiseljak and Vitez, Busovaca and Travnik, and at that time, the communication links with eastern Bosnia and southern Bosnia and the enormous influx of refugees and displaced persons had an effect on the crime rate. Crime soared, and this led to a collapse of general law and order. However, I focused my attention on the front line, and I spent sometimes several weeks and sometimes several months working out the organisation and defence and I was -- in the defence of Jajce and Travnik and other areas. I was engaged in that. The crime that took place was, first and foremost, the looting of social property, socially-owned property. At that time, as property did not have a defined owner, defined ownership, some people considered that it was quite all right, that it was moral to appropriate what was known as socially-owned property, that is to say, property owned by certain companies, social companies and so on. Then there was an appropriation of materiel from the warehouses of the former JNA, and this appropriation was done on different pretexts but the consequences of it were always the same. Then there was a general reselling of weapons and military materiel which very often led to family tragedies and a settling of accounts where profits were concerned. Then there was the formation of barricades, ad hoc barricades and roadblocks on roads, and this was a basic source of income for certain villages along the roads, main roads, in Central Bosnia. Each village took it into their own hands to set up a roadblock and a checkpoint and to reap the profits thereof, a sort of tax that they levied of their own accord, and then there was highway robbery, so to speak, and motor vehicles were confiscated and appropriated, stolen, in fact, and later on there was looting of family houses, first of all of workers who were employed abroad, that is to say, the houses were empty and their owners working abroad, but then looting of the other homes began as well. This was also done in a systematic manner, that is to say, they would even steal the construction materials, the bricks and roofs and so on, and it was a very lucrative business to evacuate citizens from Sarajevo. It was a phenomenon at that time that for the profiteers, the road was always open and that they always managed, given remuneration and if you paid them, that they would ensure the evacuation of people from Sarajevo and the encirclement around Sarajevo. This was a lucrative business. There were also other high-profit goods that were sold and imported and sold in the region. In a word, crime flourished, and it led to the breakdown of the system of law and order that had prevailed and it led to a misbalance and general destruction of all criteria, moral criteria and all others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In 1992, having given us an overview of the situation in Central Bosnia and having had an overview of the situation yourself, and you will be describing this to us, what was civilian power and authority like and what were your relationships to civilian authority? How did you distribute your authorities? Where did they coincide? So tell us something about civilian power and authority in the area of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in 1992.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In 1992, I was informed that a regional main staff existed as a coordinating body of the civilian organs of power and authority. However, I did not consider myself competent for the civilian organs of power and authority, and I did not consider them to have any competence over me. I know that my superior was the chief of the main staff and, for the most part, that is how I behaved and what my conduct was like. The civilian power and authority at the level of the municipalities functioned for the most part in an autonomous manner, and we could even say that it was a sort of state within a state, and apart from coordination, there were no other links, and these two power structures endeavoured, I say "endeavoured," to function quite separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The central authorities in Sarajevo, was their effect felt in any way in the area of Central Bosnia, either with the Croats or with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was not, and this could be seen on the basis of the daily functioning of the civilian institutions, the taxes that were levied and customs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who levied taxes and duty, customs duty?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were levied and taken in by the municipality but with regard to the population and not the area, which was a little strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does that mean? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that meant that the members of the Croatian people, for the most part, paid their dues vis-à-vis the organs of the civilian authorities of the HVO and the members of the Muslim Bosniak people paid their dues via taxes which they paid to the authorities of the Bosniak Muslim authorities in the same municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened with the legal system in 1992, the justice system, the law court system?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In 1992, at the level of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, towards the municipalities, it was not functioning for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about at the level of the municipalities; was the legal system working there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. In 1992, no civilian courts were functioning apart from an attempt to set up regional military courts, district courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Between the civil authorities -- civilian authorities in towns, for example, Muslim civilian authorities and the government in Sarajevo, was there any communication between the two which is standard practice in states of any kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, this kind of communication did not exist, but I didn't have any personal insight into that mechanism and that communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the balance of payments and the system of payments between companies and the state; did that system function as it had done before the war or did it disintegrate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't able to function because there wasn't a currency. The German mark was the prevailing currency, whereas the balance of payments and everything else was not functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the post office system; did that function in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did pensioners receive their pensions and did salaries come in to civil servants from the budget?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, only if the municipality had its own resources in order to pay these dues. They were not, in fact, pensions but they were just -- they just took care of the social cases. People who relied on social welfare to survive, they would receive remuneration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the pension funds from Sarajevo? Did they send pensions to people or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened to money and currency? What was the money that was in use in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the German mark was the prevailing currency at that time in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was the valid currency for the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You could buy and sell on the basis of the German mark throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What currency was proclaimed by the government in Sarajevo as the prevailing currency?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For a time, the Yugoslavia dinar was the currency in use, but it had devalued a great deal. Later on, there was bonds of some kind and 1992, and only later on did the BH dinar come into play, it was introduced, the BH dinar, but it was impossible to buy anything because there were no goods to buy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was Croatian kuna also used in this area of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was because -- this was forced by the circumstances, because in order to buy goods, you had to go to the first neighbouring store or the first neighbouring country, and so the Croatian kuna was also used.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At that time, according to the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was there an army; in other words, what was the legal armed force in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Yugolav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So that was the army with which at least two ethnic groups were at war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the case with the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can speak about Central Bosnia. In at least eleven municipalities, the civilian police had ceased to exist. The central links, that is, links with certain centres, had been maintained, but according to the information I received from the chief of the Kiseljak police station, he issued the last salary to his staff in April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo. Ordinarily we would go until a quarter to six, but since -- well, perhaps we could go for another five or six minutes, but I would like us to settle this problem that I raised with you a while back about the common interests between the Aleksovski and Blaskic Trial Chambers. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
