utterances.text: Shall I go till about 5.45, or shall I cut it off a bit earlier so that we can discuss the Aleksovski issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go for another five minutes, then we'll stop, and we'll use the last five minutes to discuss the problem that I mentioned so that we don't keep the interpreters any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you just described some key functions of the federal state, and you said that they did not operate. So who filled in this void; in other words, who regulated life in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This void, for the most part by force, was filled in by the municipality which took over all these functions and attempted to discharge them in addition to all the other functions which it had legally. So this was simply a situation which we had, that each municipality functioned as a mini state in itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So let's list other functions: police, taxing, schools. Who was regulating these affairs which used to be regulated by the state?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All this was done by the municipality. What the school year was going to be, when school would start and when it would finish; police affairs, the size of the police force, the active police force size; and many, many other activities, levying of taxes, other income, supplying the citizenship, that is, the entire economy, the police, even the defence; in good part, the defence as well, because the municipality was the main logistics base for the military conscripts because the municipality also carried out tax of mobilisation which was a competence of the state, and all the mobilisation plans were drafted by the municipality, that is, competent departments of the municipal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the competence of the municipality sort of overlap with the competences of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone which you led?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they overlapped, and the municipalities de facto had a large number of competences which were, in fact, competences of the command of the Operative Zone, at least in theory, on paper, but which were to be taken over from the municipal structures by the regional headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are still talking about 1992. We will move on to 1993 later. But in 1992 were you trying to take over the rest, so to speak, some of the competences which they had which you felt that you had, and could you mention some of the issues over which you wrested with them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There were activities there and, of course, I tried to take over the competences which were a part of commanding. Let me give you one example only: The municipal crisis staffs adopted a decision on the involvement of troops, even to the point that at a level of local communes, the municipal crisis staffs adopted decisions on the involvement of troops. They appointed commanders and also regulated compensation, the distribution of logistics such as ammunition. All this was within the competences of the municipalities because they controlled the means with which this equipment or this materiel was acquired. Similarly with respect to the combat operations and the logistics support for these combat operations because the logistics affairs, the mobilisation affairs, and even the establishment affairs were conducted by the municipal structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you agree, I think we have reached the end of a particular area, so this may be a good point where we can stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We'll stop at that point and we'll resume tomorrow, remember at 9.45, Friday. Friday is tomorrow. All right. Mr. Prosecutor, have you consulted with your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have, Mr. President, Your Honours, and we certainly have no objection to Judge Rodrigues participating in any decision taken on the motion that has been presented by the Aleksovski Chamber to this particular Trial Chamber. So we agree to his participating in the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Hayman or Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, we consent to Judge Rodrigues acting as a member of the Trial Chamber on this issue. I'm not sure you need our consent; he is a member of the Trial Chamber. As a footnote, the Defence notes that we don't know who the protected witness is that the Aleksovski Trial Chamber has -- well, perhaps the Appellate Chamber now has ordered the transcript to be made available in the other case. We don't know if it's a Prosecution witness or a Defence witness, I think. I have read the appellate decision that was made available to us yesterday, and I think that's the only paper ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think only the Prosecutor knows. I don't know. I don't think Judge Shahabuddeen does either, nor does the Aleksovski case. The problem here was simply to know how the Trial Chamber should be composed. Now that the trial has been composed, thanks to your agreement, we ourselves can know to what extent we can or cannot modify the protective measures that were taken, but in general, you should know -- I think we can say, the decision was public -- you should already know the direction that the Blaskic Chamber has taken, that is, to strengthen or at least not to diminish the protection of witnesses once the testimonies move from one case to another. Having said that, it's with pleasure and satisfaction that we have noted the agreement of the parties and that the Trial Chamber be definitively composed as it is with Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The only footnote, Mr. President, I was making was if the witness was a Defence witness, a protected Defence witness, we do not consent without further discussion or information to the revelation of a protected Defence witness to another party, including -- to another party, period. But I don't know if the witness the Prosecutor seeks is a protected Defence witness or a protected Prosecution witness. If we could be told the pseudonym, if it was a pseudonymed witness in our case, then we already know who it is based on the pseudonym, and we may well be in a position to consent. Even if it were a Defence witness, I just want to note we don't know that. We're operating a little bit in the dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman, but you're really going now to the substance of the motion. We simply had to know who was going to decide, whether it would be with two Judges or three Judges, but as concerns the rest, I don't know whether Mr. Harmon wants to tell us something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can assuage my colleague's concerns. It is a Prosecution witness. I won't say more and I will not identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That probably does eliminate any concern. There may be cases where there are Prosecution witnesses and there were segments of the testimony that the Defence had a unique interest in the sealed nature or confidential nature of a question or a document. I don't know. But subject to that, we, of course, would not have any objection and would consent to whatever the Court feels appropriate with respect to confidential Prosecution witness material. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. It's with satisfaction that Judge Shahabuddeen and I accept Judge Rodrigues on this very sensitive issue. Thank you very much. The court stands adjourned, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.47 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of February, 1999, at 9.45 a.m.
